Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

sheepdog (development version)

  • export_occupancy_data() exports a calibration on continuous covariates of the occasion (tp ~ logit_conf + temp_z), schema sheepdog-occupancy 1.3: P(TP) is computed for each prediction, the versions of the detections are drawn in the export and written to occasion_draws.parquet, and calibration_draws.parquet is not written. schema.json records the covariates (calibration$covariates), their range in the calibration data and their standardisation (covariate_scaling). New arguments n_versions, rule, p_min and covariate_scaling; without covariates, n_versions calls occasion_draws() on the folder (schema 1.2). occasion_draws() refuses a folder of schema 1.3, which has no grid. New fixture tests/testthat/fixtures/export-1.3, checked by the contract test. Agreed with crywolf (dev/proposal-calibration-covariates.md there), which will read version 1.3 later.
  • calibration_prior() gives other population-level terms, such as a continuous covariate, a normal(0, 1) prior; the slope of logit_conf then keeps normal(1, 1) without the truncation at 0, since ‘brms’ cannot bound a single coefficient.
  • New covariate_bins() cuts a covariate of the occasions (an environmental gradient, such as the temperature of the night, or an acoustic index of the recording or minute) into bins, by default quantiles within each site. select_clips() gains covariates, so that the "random_detections" draw can be stratified by those bins (strata = "temp_bin") with exact inclusion probabilities, and a message recalls that a stratum related to the verdict should enter the calibration. precision_by_bin(), suggest_thresholds() and cell_status() gain by, to check each site x species cell within the bins. vignette("validation-effort") has a new section, “Stage 1 along a gradient”, with both examples and their caveats.
  • man/sheepdog-package.Rd lists the three authors (it was not regenerated when Authors@R changed).
  • vignette("crywolf-integration"): the Curiango data come from seven recorders, not four, and the calibration model is chosen among three candidates, not two.
  • Larissa S. M. Sugai and Liliana Piatti, who designed the validation protocol, are now listed as authors (Authors@R and CITATION.cff).
  • New export_occupancy_data() writes, in one folder, the data of an occupancy model with false positives (schema sheepdog-occupancy, version 1): every occasion, with or without predictions (occasions.csv), the predictions above min_confidence (detections.csv) and their highest score per occasion x species (scores.csv), the reviewed clips with their design and inclusion probability (validation.csv), the recordings annotated by ear (recordings_verified.csv), the site covariates (sites.csv) and, with a model fitted with engine = "brms", posterior draws of P(TP) on a grid of scores (calibration_draws.parquet). schema.json records the version of the schema and the settings of the export. vignette("crywolf-integration") documents every column.
  • ‘jsonlite’ is imported and ‘arrow’ is suggested, for the export.
  • export_occupancy_data() drops predictions that repeat the site, recording, offset and species of another (e.g. a selection table read twice), with a warning, and warns when most occasion x species with several predictions share a single score, a sign that one score per occasion was copied to several rows.
  • export_occupancy_data() writes version 1.1 of the sheepdog-occupancy schema, which only adds to version 1: occasion_covariates appends covariates of the occasions (matched by occasion_id or by recording) to occasions.csv, and calibration_keys exports a calibration that depends on a property of the occasion, such as the month (tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | month)): each key becomes a text column of occasions.csv and of calibration_draws.parquet, which covers every level found among the occasions (levels absent from the calibration data are drawn as new levels). schema.json lists them in occasion_covariates and calibration$keys. A small export of the example data in this schema, made by data-raw/make_export_fixture.R, is shared with crywolf as a test fixture.
  • New occasion_draws() turns an export with calibration draws into one version of the detection data per posterior draw: in each draw an occasion is a detection when at least one of its predictions is judged true, either at random with its probability of being true ("sample") or above p_min ("threshold"). It writes occasion_draws.parquet in the export (schema version 1.2), so that any occupancy software can propagate the uncertainty of the calibration. The random numbers follow those of crywolf::fp_draws_data(), and a test checks that both give the same detections; tests/testthat/fixtures/export-1.2/ holds the shared case.
  • vignette("crywolf-integration") runs the whole flow on the Curiango data (one-minute recordings, two classifiers): export, posterior predictive check of the calibration, occasion_draws() and the Monte Carlo propagation in crywolf (fp_draws_data(), fp_occu_mc()), with results cached in inst/benchmarks/curiango-flow-*.csv.
  • A contract test (tests/testthat/test-contract.R, the counterpart of crywolf’s test-read_sheepdog.R) checks that exports follow the schema documented in vignette("crywolf-integration"): the fields of schema.json and the row counts it declares, the columns and keys of every table, scores.csv against detections.csv, calibration keys as text covering every level of the occasions, and the layout of occasion_draws.parquet. With crywolf installed, it also checks that crywolf reads each export and the stored occasion draws.
  • New calibration_ppc() checks a Bayesian calibration model against the reviewed clips: the observed share of true positives against its posterior predictive distribution, overall and by score bin, site, species and any column of the validation data (e.g. month), with a mid-p Bayesian p-value. plot_calibration_ppc() draws one check.
  • vignette("sampling-designs") gains a section on recorders that run the classifier on the device and discard the audio: keep a probability sample of the raw audio, drawn without looking at the scores, so that the calibration and the false-positive rate can still be estimated.
  • The v1.2.0 reproduction test compares the auc_sd column of the effort curve with a relative tolerance of 1e-2 (1e-3 elsewhere): with lme4 2.1-0 this standard deviation over three small fits moves by about 0.4%.

sheepdog 3.2.1

  • Added fast tests for posterior matrix uncertainty, training provenance, overlap boundaries, missing clips and degenerate reviewer agreement.
  • Corrected the minimum dplyr version for join relationship checks.
  • Fixed the performance article index and replaced an unresolved manuscript DOI link with the validated Zenodo data citation.
  • Declared the repositories needed by the optional crywolf integration in Additional_repositories for CRAN checks.

sheepdog 3.2.0

  • calibration_models(single_species = TRUE) provides global and site- effect candidates for one species, including an optional uncorrelated site-slope model. calibrate() and compare_calibration_models() automatically choose candidates from the observed species and sites; explicit model lists still override automatic selection in the latter. The multispecies candidate family and its ordering are unchanged.
  • New performance vignette summarises the Curiango benchmark, regression checks and a reproducible multispecies simulation with held-out nights.

sheepdog 3.1.0

  • cell_status() includes both observed score endpoints in its grid and never extrapolates below the reviewed minimum. Crossings between 0.99 and the reviewed maximum are no longer missed.
  • New calibration_folds() exposes reproducible fold assignments. compare_calibration_models() and calibrate() accept fold_group, e.g. "source_audio" or "night", to keep groups intact across species within a site. The default clip assignment is unchanged.
  • read_validations(keep = ) optionally retains grouping metadata; calibrate() requests it automatically and saves grouped assignments in calibration_folds.csv. Missing IDs and insufficient groups raise clear errors. Single-verdict test folds retain probability scores and have missing AUC without counting as failed fits.

sheepdog 3.0.0

Breaking changes

  • calibrate() and select_calibration_model() now default to "one_se_logloss": choose the simplest candidate within one standard error of the lowest cross-validated log-loss, excluding candidates singular in most folds unless all are singular (with a warning). Supply select = "best_auc" (or rule = "best_auc" in the selector) to retain the 2.x selection. The comparison table still reports all metrics and is ordered by AUC; its first row is not necessarily the selected model. See the migration guide for a reproducible example.

Documentation and infrastructure

  • Added the 2.x to 3.0.0 migration guide.
  • CI measures test coverage with covr and uploads an HTML report and Cobertura XML as workflow artifacts, without a third-party token.

Documentation

  • New article “Reviewing clips in the BirdNET GUI” (site only): the review in the Review tab of the BirdNET-Analyzer GUI, from the folder of clips to the Positive and Negative folders read by classify_review(), with screenshots in English and Portuguese (where the result folders are positivo and negativo), the regression panel of the GUI compared with the calibration of stage 2, and the review with several reviewers.

Sampling

  • select_clips(strata = ) gains the presets "hour" (pooling the nights), "week" (ISO week of the night) and "month", and accepts a character vector of column names for strata defined by the user, e.g. c("month", "moon") with a column added to the detections before the call. site and species_code are always added to the strata, columns that depend on the score (confidence, rank) are refused, and every stratum column must be constant within an occasion.

Calibration

  • fit_calibration() (and calibrate()) passes on the messages of lme4::glmer(), prefixed by lme4:, instead of hiding them; the message on singular fits is not repeated, since it already becomes a warning. Every message of the fit is kept in the attribute sheepdog_messages of the model, and calibrate() appends them to calibration_model.txt. The fits of the cross-validation folds and of the effort curve stay quiet.

sheepdog 2.2.0

Calibration

  • compare_calibration_models() also scores the predicted probabilities on the held-out folds: log-loss and Brier score (proper scoring rules), calibration intercept and slope, the share of singular fold fits (prop_singular) and the position of each model (complexity).
  • New select_calibration_model(), with the rules "best_auc" (the rule of 2.x) and "one_se_logloss" (the simplest model within one standard error of the lowest log-loss, leaving out singular fits). calibrate() takes the rule in select; the default stays "best_auc" until 3.0.0, when it becomes "one_se_logloss".
  • calibration_models(uncorrelated = TRUE) adds m5_species_x_site_uncorrelated, the m4 structure without the correlation between the species intercepts and slopes, which avoids the singular fits of m4; calibrate() takes it with uncorrelated = TRUE.

Bayesian calibration

  • fit_calibration() gains engine = "brms": the model is fitted with ‘brms’ (Bernoulli, logit link). The prior must be given explicitly. Convergence diagnostics run after the fit and warn when R-hat, the effective sample sizes or the divergent transitions fail the usual limits.
  • New calibration_prior(): a weakly informative example prior centred on an already calibrated score (slope 1, intercept at the mean logit score), with the slope truncated at 0, exponential(1) on the standard deviations and lkj(2) on the correlations; only the classes present in the formula are returned.
  • New prior_predictive_calibration() and plot_calibration_draws() for prior predictive checks and for the uncertainty of the fitted curve; calibration_diagnostics(); calibration_sensitivity(), a power-scaling sensitivity analysis with ‘priorsense’.
  • score_detections() with a ‘brms’ model computes the posterior on a grid of scores per site x species and returns p_tp (posterior mean), p_tp_lower and pr_reliable (posterior probability that P(TP) >= p_min).
  • detection_history() gains rule = c("mean", "probability") and prob_min: a detection is reliable when its posterior mean reaches p_min, or when pr_reliable reaches prob_min.
  • New history_draws() and community_matrices_draws(): the detection histories and the community matrices over posterior draws, with the posterior mean and an interval for each cell.
  • calibrate() gains engine, prior (a prior or a function of the selected formula, such as calibration_prior), brms_args, rule and prob_min; with ‘brms’ it also writes calibration_diagnostics.csv.
  • New vignette("bayesian-calibration"), precomputed.
  • ‘brms’, ‘posterior’ and ‘priorsense’ are suggested packages.

Sampling

  • select_clips() gains strata ("night_hour", the rule of 2.0.0, "night" or "site_species") for the occasion draw of "random_detections". With one recording per hour, the default stratum holds a single occasion and draws nothing; a coarser stratum makes the draw random. A coarser stratum combined with balance_by_hour = TRUE under a target or limit warns that inclusion_prob is conditional on the first draw.
  • extract_validation_clips() writes extraction_info.csv with the provenance of the run (date, versions of sheepdog and R, folder of the tables, the new classifier label and every argument of select_clips()).
  • The message on predictions dropped by min_confidence is no longer printed when none is dropped.

Review and retraining

  • New read_validation_tables(): stacks the validation_by_clip.csv tables of several sites or rounds with every column and verdict (unlike read_validations(), which keeps only what the calibration needs).
  • New build_training_set(): copies the reviewed clips into the training layout of BirdNET-Analyzer (positives in <species_code>/, negatives in -<species_code>/), with the sites in test_sites in a separate test folder for --test_data; writes training_set.csv and warns about classes with fewer positive files than min_files.
  • New exclude_training_clips(): drops from a manifest the clips that overlap a clip used in training (same species and recording).
  • vignette("retraining") uses the new functions.

Community matrices

  • New cell_status(): classifies each site x species cell of the calibration as "reliable" (the calibrated curve reaches p_min within the reviewed scores, with at least min_n clips), "probably_absent" (no true positive among the reviewed clips) or "unreliable", separating the absence of a species from a calibration that fails.
  • New suggest_core_species(): the species with no unreliable cell.
  • community_matrices() gains drop_empty (drop the site x month rows without any core species) and returns trials, the matrix of nights recorded with the dimensions of the species counts, for the Ntrials of a binomial model such as gllvm::gllvm().
  • vignette("community-matrices") uses the new functions.

Several reviewers

  • New assign_reviewers(): splits the clips of a manifest among reviewers, balanced within species, with a fraction (overlap) given to a second reviewer.
  • New split_by_reviewer(): copies each reviewer’s clips to their own folder tree for the BirdNET GUI.
  • New reviewer_agreement(): agreement and kappa per species on the clips reviewed more than once (Cohen’s kappa for two reviewers, Fleiss’ kappa otherwise).
  • New consensus_verdicts(): one verdict per clip; conflicting clips get verdict = "disagreement" and are left out of precision and calibration.

sheepdog 2.1.0

Bug fixes

  • classify_review() classified the clips wrongly on Windows when review_dir had backslashes (e.g. E:\validation\clips): the name of the review folder entered the search for the verdict, so a folder named after a verdict marked every clip with it.

Warnings and diagnostics

  • fit_calibration() warns when the fitted GLMM is singular (a variance estimated at zero or a correlation at +-1); calibrate() passes the warning on.
  • compare_calibration_models() warns about, and counts in the new column n_failed, the folds whose fit failed; before, they were silently left out of the mean AUC.
  • calibration_effort() warns when n_train exceeds the smallest site x species cell minus five, and returns n_train_mean, n_test_mean and n_failed.
  • The documentation of select_clips() explains that target_total gives rare species higher inclusion probabilities (weight pooled estimates by 1 / inclusion_prob) and that the default recording_fraction = 0.01 draws one recording per site in small projects.

Documentation

  • New articles, run on a simulated example data set: vignette("sheepdog") (Get started), vignette("sampling-designs"), vignette("validation-effort"), vignette("calibration"), vignette("community-matrices") and vignette("retraining") (training folders for BirdNET-Analyzer from the reviewed clips).
  • The example data set (4 sites x 8 species x 6 months; selection tables, the list of recordings, reviewed clips and a calibrated nightly history) ships in system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog"); data-raw/make_example_data.R generates it.
  • plot_precision() draws one line per site when the table has several sites; before, the lines of different sites were joined in the same panel (also in the precision_by_bin.png of post_validation()).
  • vignette("community-matrices") uses a PCoA on square-root Bray-Curtis (ape::pcoa()) and a binomial GLLVM (‘gllvm’) for a model-based ordination and a test of the season effect; ‘ape’, ‘gllvm’ and ‘vegan’ are suggested packages, used only there.
  • The vignette crywolf-contract is now crywolf-integration (“Integration with crywolf”).
  • The repository was renamed to diogoprov/sheepdog; the package site is https://provetelab.org/sheepdog/.
  • The package can be installed from r-universe (install.packages("sheepdog", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))), with binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux.

Tests

  • The comparisons with the v1.2.0 outputs tolerate floating-point differences between platforms (relative tolerance 1e-3 for the calibration outputs, 1e-8 for the others); R CMD check runs on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu in GitHub Actions.

sheepdog 2.0.0

The four scripts of birdnet-validation-sampler v1.2.0 become the R package sheepdog. With the same settings and seed, the package writes the same tables as v1.2.0, after the renaming below; the test suite checks this against outputs of the v1.2.0 scripts on simulated data. The scripts are preserved in the v1.2.0 tag.

From scripts to functions

v1.2.0 script sheepdog
extrair_clipes_validacao.R extract_validation_clips(); steps read_selection_tables(), select_clips(), cut_clips(), pack_clips()
pos_validacao.R post_validation(); steps classify_review(), precision_by_bin(), suggest_thresholds(), nightly_presence(), retraining_clips(), plot_precision()
calibracao.R calibrate(); steps read_validations(), calibration_models(), compare_calibration_models(), fit_calibration(), calibration_effort(), score_detections(), detection_history(), summarise_history(), plot_calibration()
gerar_matrizes_comunidade.R build_community_matrices(); step community_matrices()

select_clips() is a pure function: it returns the clip manifest without reading or writing audio.

Settings become arguments

Defaults are those of the config blocks, except project paths and project-specific lists, which are now required arguments (or NULL).

Output files, columns and values in English

  • Files: manifesto_clipes.csv → clip_manifest.csv; validacao_por_clipe.csv → validation_by_clip.csv; precisao_por_faixa → precision_by_bin; thresholds_sugeridos → suggested_thresholds; presenca_por_noite → nightly_presence; clipes_para_retreino → retraining_clips; comparacao_modelos → model_comparison; modelo_calibracao → calibration_model; curvas_calibradas → calibration_curves; curva_esforco → effort_curve; deteccoes_calibradas_<local> → calibrated_detections_<site>; historico_deteccao_noite → nightly_detection_history; resumo_deteccao_especie_local → detection_summary; matriz_frequencia_local_mes_k<k> → frequency_matrix_site_month_k<k>; matriz_contagens_local_mes_k<k> → count_matrix_site_month_k<k>; esforco_local_mes → effort_site_month. Folders clipes/ and pacotes/ → clips/ and packages/.
  • Columns and values of the manifest and the validation table: see vignette("crywolf-contract"). Other columns: especie → species, data → date, hora → hour, n_deteccoes → n_detections, n_confiaveis → n_reliable, deteccao(_k1..k3) → detection(_k1..k3), faixa → bin, n_validados → n_reviewed, n_positivos → n_positive, precisao → precision, pouco_suporte → low_support, n_suporte → n_support, precisao_no_corte → precision_at_threshold, n_clipes → n_clips, presenca → presence (confirmed, not_detected_in_reviewed, not_reviewed), conf_max_positivo → max_confidence_positive, modelo → model, auc_media/auc_dp → auc_mean/auc_sd, n_por_celula → n_per_cell, noites(_k1..k3) → nights(_k1..k3), mes → month, n_noites_gravadas → n_nights_recorded, incluido → included, n_noites_deteccao → n_nights_detected, frequencia → frequency.
  • Calibration models: m1_int_especie → m1_species_intercept, m2_slope_especie → m2_species_slope, m3_mais_local → m3_plus_site, m4_especie_x_local → m4_species_x_site; the model terms use species and site.
  • Whole-recording clips are named rec_... instead of grav_....
  • Messages, warnings and errors are in English.

Reading v1.2.0 files

post_validation(), classify_review(), calibrate(), read_validations(), community_matrices() and build_community_matrices() read manifests, validation tables and histories written by v1.2.0 and rename them on reading, so validated data stay usable.

Changes in behaviour

  • Random draws use withr::with_seed(): the draws are those of v1.2.0, and the global random number generator is left as it was.
  • suggest_thresholds() returns an empty table when no reviewed clip has a confidence score (whole recordings only); v1.2.0 wrote a row of NA.
  • The verdict patterns of the review are case-insensitive and only match the subfolders below review_dir, not the review folder itself.
  • A manifest without a confidence column is accepted.
  • score_detections() warns about prediction tables named after a site that is not in the calibration, and keeps the site name in the output.
  • The random-effects models of the calibration need ‘lme4’, and the package now stops when it is missing instead of letting those fits fail.
  • ‘av’, ‘lme4’ and ‘ggplot2’ are suggested packages, needed only to cut audio, to fit hierarchical models and to draw the figures.
